collection.description: A villager works harder than anyone in the village.

ask.text:
(subject) works harder than anyone in the village. First up, last to bed, never takes a day off, and can't understand people who do. (subject.His/her) family worry. (subject.He/She) has stopped coming to the fire in the evenings, and (subject.his/her) hands shake when (subject.he/she) eats.
(apprentice), the healers' youngest apprentice, has made something to help: a little cake of crushed sleeping-flowers and honey, which (apprentice.he/she) says will "slow (subject.him/her) down a bit." (apprentice.He/She) hasn't tested it. (apprentice.He/She) is very hopeful. (subject)'s family have hidden it in (subject)'s supper.
(subject) has noticed the supper tastes of honey. Should (subject.he/she) eat it anyway, or push it away?

c1o1.text: (subject) sleeps for a day and a half. When (subject.he/she) wakes, (subject.he/she) feels better than (subject.he/she) has in years, and the idea of working from dark to dark seems silly. (subject.He/She) still works. (subject.He/She) just stops when (subject.he/she) is tired now, and comes to the fire in the evenings, and laughs. (subject.His/her) family send (apprentice) a basket of fruit.

c1o2.text: (subject) sleeps for three days. When (subject.he/she) wakes, (subject.he/she) is very calm about everything. Very, very calm. Jobs get done when they get done. Things that used to bother (subject.him/her) don't bother (subject.him/her) at all. (subject.His/her) family are relieved, then slightly alarmed. (apprentice) writes "half the honey" on (apprentice.his/her) recipe.

c1.text: (subject) eats every bite, too tired to argue. Then (subject.he/she) sits back, and the fire seems very warm, and the voices round it very kind, and (subject.his/her) eyelids very heavy...

c2o1.text: In the end (subject)'s family just tell (subject.him/her) why. That they're worried. That (subject.his/her) hands shake. That they miss (subject.him/her) at the fire. (subject) says nothing for a long time. Then (subject.he/she) eats the cake, just to be polite, and stays at the fire till the end, and it's the start of something.

c2o2.text: (apprentice), offended that (apprentice.his/her) cake is being refused, eats it (apprentice.himself/herself) to prove it's safe. (apprentice.He/She) falls asleep sitting up, falls sideways into the woodpile, and wakes up two days later with a lump on (apprentice.his/her) head and a very sore arm. (subject) goes on working from dark to dark.

c2.text: "Someone's put something in this," says (subject), and pushes the bowl across the mat. Everyone round the fire looks innocent. (apprentice) looks so innocent (apprentice.he/she) goes red...
